props.gloss_en: the plain sense of the mishna's verse (Joel 2:23): the first rain and the last rain are in the first month (Nisan)
the first rain is in Marcheshvan and the last rain in Nisan
R' Yochanan: this verse was fulfilled in the days of Joel son of Pethuel, the year of which it is written 'what the gazam left the locust ate' (Joel 1:4)
that year Adar ended with no rain, and the first rainfall fell on the first of Nisan
the prophet told Israel to go and sow; they asked whether one with a kav of wheat or two of barley should eat and live or sow and die; he said: nevertheless go and sow
a miracle was done for them: what was in the walls and in the ant holes was revealed to them
they sowed on the 2nd-4th, the second rainfall came on the 5th of Nisan, and the omer on the 16th came from grain that grew in eleven days instead of six months
of that generation it says: 'they who sow in tears shall reap in joy; he goes weeping, bearing the measure of seed' (Ps 126:5-6)
[the stam asks the meaning of 'he goes weeping'] R' Yehuda: the ox goes weeping as it plows, and on its return eats the shoots from the furrow -- that is 'he shall come in joy'
[the stam asks the meaning of 'bearing his sheaves'] the stalk was a span and the ear two spans

[RN: in the seven years of famine (II Kings 8:1), what did they eat?] R' Yochanan: year by year -- what was in the houses, the fields, clean animals, unclean animals, vermin, their children, and in the seventh the flesh of their own arms
the seventh year fulfils what is stated: 'each man shall eat the flesh of his own arm' (Isaiah 9:19)

[RN: 'it is holy in your midst, and I will not enter the city' (Hosea 11:9) -- because it is holy He will not enter?] R' Yochanan: the Holy One said: I will not enter Jerusalem above until I enter Jerusalem below
the stam: yes, there is a Jerusalem above, as it is written 'Jerusalem built as a city joined together' (Ps 122:3)
[RN: Jer 10:8?] R' Yochanan: 'one' is the sin that burns the wicked in Gehinnom -- idolatry; 'hevel' here (Jer 10:8) and 'hevel' there of idols (Jer 10:15)
the verse 'there': 'they are vanity, a work of delusion' (Jer 10:15), said of idols
[RN: 'my people have done two evils' (Jer 2:13) -- only two? were the twenty-four left aside?] R' Yochanan: one that weighs as two, and that is idolatry
as it is written (Jer 2:13), and it is written of them (Jer 2:10-11): has a nation exchanged its gods... but My people has exchanged its glory
a tanna: the Kittim worship fire and Kedar water, and though they know water quenches fire they did not exchange their gods -- 'and My people has exchanged its glory'
the plain sense of the verse (I Sam 8:1): Samuel grew old
the Master: one who dies at fifty-two -- that is the death of Samuel of Rama (so Samuel died at 52)
R' Yochanan: old age sprang upon him, as it is written 'I regret that I made Saul king' (I Sam 15:11)
[in R' Yochanan's narrative] Samuel before God: You weighed me as Moses and Aaron (Ps 99:6); as their handiwork was not annulled in their lifetime, let mine not be annulled in mine

[in R' Yochanan's narrative] the Holy One: Saul cannot die (Samuel would not allow it), Samuel cannot die young (people would murmur), and neither can live on -- David's reign has arrived, and one reign does not touch another even by a hair's breadth

the Holy One: I will spring old age upon him. That is 'and Saul sat in Gibeah under the tamarisk in Rama' (I Sam 22:6) -- what caused Saul to sit in Gibeah two and a half years? the prayer of Samuel of Rama
R' Yochanan: 'I have slain them by the words of My mouth' (Hosea 6:5) -- not 'by their deeds' but 'by the words of My mouth'
the stam: yes -- one man is set aside before another
[RN at the meal: let the master say something] R' Yochanan: one does not converse at a meal, lest the windpipe precede the gullet and he come into danger
R' Yochanan [after the meal]: our father Jacob did not die
Rav Nachman: was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried?
R' Yitzchak: whoever says 'Rachav, Rachav' immediately has an emission
Rav Nachman: I say it and it does not affect me
R' Yitzchak: when I said it, [I meant] one who knew her and recognised her

R' Yitzchak's parable: a hungry, tired, thirsty traveller in the desert finds a tree with sweet fruit, pleasant shade and a stream beneath; leaving, he says: with what shall I bless you? -- may all saplings planted from you be like you
R' Yitzchak to Rav Nachman: so you -- Torah, wealth and children you have; rather, may it be His will that your offspring be like you
